The original deleteMany was intentionally restricted to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` because the SMS scheduling cron is the only owner of those rows; EMAIL/WHATSAPP reminders have their own cron paths. With this change, ANY WorkflowReminder row with retryCount > 1 will be deleted by this SMS handler, regardless of method. Today only this file increments retryCount, so there is no immediate data loss, but the cleanup now silently reaches across reminder types and will cause unexpected deletions the moment retryCount is reused for EMAIL or WHATSAPP elsewhere. Scope the clause to `{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`."

      "body": "The try block can throw from the success-path `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ scheduled: true, referenceId: scheduledSMS.sid })` (lines 169-177) AFTER `twilio.scheduleSMS` has already returned a truthy result and Twilio has accepted the message. The catch handler then unconditionally increments retryCount. Consequence: retryCount grows on a row whose Twilio message is already scheduled, and because `scheduled` is still false in the DB the next cron run will call `twilio.scheduleSMS` again, producing a duplicate SMS to the user. The retryCount bump must only happen when the Twilio call itself failed (or returned falsy), not when the bookkeeping update of an already-scheduled reminder fails."

If that update fails (e.g. the row was concurrently deleted by another worker, or a transient DB error) the exception escapes the for-loop and the request returns 500 before processing the remaining reminders in `unscheduledReminders`. Wrap the catch-block update in its own try/catch (or log-and-continue) so one failed update cannot skip the rest of the batch."

findings.title: retryCount-based deleteMany is not scoped to SMS method
findings.body: The new OR branch `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` in the cleanup deleteMany does not filter by `method`. The original deleteMany was intentionally restricted to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` because the SMS scheduling cron is the only owner of those rows; EMAIL/WHATSAPP reminders have their own cron paths. With this change, ANY WorkflowReminder row with retryCount > 1 will be deleted by this SMS handler, regardless of method. Today only this file increments retryCount, so there is no immediate data loss, but the cleanup now silently reaches across reminder types and will cause unexpected deletions the moment retryCount is reused for EMAIL or WHATSAPP elsewhere. Scope the clause to `{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`.

findings.title: Catch block increments retryCount after Twilio already accepted the SMS
findings.body: The try block can throw from the success-path `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ scheduled: true, referenceId: scheduledSMS.sid })` (lines 169-177) AFTER `twilio.scheduleSMS` has already returned a truthy result and Twilio has accepted the message. The catch handler then unconditionally increments retryCount. Consequence: retryCount grows on a row whose Twilio message is already scheduled, and because `scheduled` is still false in the DB the next cron run will call `twilio.scheduleSMS` again, producing a duplicate SMS to the user. The retryCount bump must only happen when the Twilio call itself failed (or returned falsy), not when the bookkeeping update of an already-scheduled reminder fails.

findings.title: Scheduling failures logged via console.log instead of console.error
findings.body: The catch handler at line 198 logs the error with `console.log`, so in production this surfaces at the same severity as the routine info logs. Should be `console.error` so the failure is captured by the standard error pipeline (and the message includes the booking/reminder id, not just the raw error object).

findings.title: Unhandled throw from catch-block update aborts the rest of the cron batch
findings.body: The catch block performs a `prisma.workflowReminder.update` that is not itself wrapped in a try/catch. If that update fails (e.g. the row was concurrently deleted by another worker, or a transient DB error) the exception escapes the for-loop and the request returns 500 before processing the remaining reminders in `unscheduledReminders`. Wrap the catch-block update in its own try/catch (or log-and-continue) so one failed update cannot skip the rest of the batch.

findings.title: No tests added for the new retryCount behaviour
findings.body: The PR changes observable behaviour (WorkflowReminder rows are now deleted after 2 failed schedule attempts, and the new retryCount column drives that decision), but ships no unit or integration tests. At minimum the following cases should be covered: (1) twilio.scheduleSMS returns falsy -> retryCount incremented to 1, row preserved; (2) two consecutive falsy returns -> row deleted by the next cron run; (3) twilio.scheduleSMS throws -> retryCount incremented via the catch path; (4) twilio.scheduleSMS throws AND subsequent update throws -> loop continues for the remaining reminders. Without these the retry semantics can silently regress.
